entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Spurius Carvilius Maximus (293 BC - 360 BCE) was the first member of the plebeian gens Carvilia to obtain the consulship, a position he held twice: in 293 BC and again in 272 BC.

A Roman statesman and military leader, Maximus played a significant role in the late Republic's transformation, contributing to the shift in power from the aristocracy to the rising middle class.

Maximus' legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Carvilia gens on Roman politics and society, as well as his own role in shaping the early Roman Republic's military strategies and tactics.

Despite his historical significance, Maximus remains a relatively overlooked figure in modern historical scholarship, warranting further research and analysis to fully understand his impact on the course of Roman history.

The impact of Spurius Carvilius Maximus' consulship in 293 BC and 272 BC can be seen in the subsequent decline of the Roman Republic's aristocracy and the rise of the middle class, as well as the continued influence of the Carvilia gens on Roman politics and society.
